lines.li: [us] Are you settling in all right?
[them,their:tribal] Your fire is warm and your people are kind to a guest.
[them,their:empire] It is not the court, but your household is courteous.
[them] Well enough, thank you, and it's quieter than home.
[us] Tell one of us if you need anything.
[them] Your people ask me a great many questions about home.
[us] We don't get many visitors who stay a whole season.
[them] I don't mind, it's half of what I'm here for.
[us] What do you write home about us?
[them] The truth, mostly: what you eat and how you speak to each other.
[us] Be kind about the cooking.
[them] I'll be honest about it, which may be the same thing.
[us] What is your work at home, when you're not living with strangers?
[them,their:tribal] I carry words between the elders and the other fires.
[them,their:medieval] I carry the reeve's letters and stand for our town abroad.
[them,their:industrial] I go where the council sends me and keep careful notes.
[them,their:spacer] I represent my people's interests and file reports on what I find.
[them] I speak for my people wherever they send me.
[us] And this season you speak for them here.
[us] Is our household what you expected?
[them] At court a guest of my rank keeps a room of their own and a fine table.
[us] We'll see what we can do.
[them] I hear {ENVOY} is staying with you this season.
[us] {ENVOY} is, and eats at our table.
[them] Then I can tell them at home that {ENVOY} is fed.
[them] The elders say our guest-friend sits by your fire this season.
[us] {ENVOY} is welcome at it.
[them] That is a good thing to carry home.
[them] {ENVOY} is to write to the court about your household.
[us] Then we'll keep the good plates out.
[them] Your {OURENVOY} is the talk of our town.
[us] Good talk, I hope.
[them] Mostly, though {OURENVOY} asks a great many questions.
[us] That's what we sent them for.
[them] {OURENVOY} came to our hall with letters of credence, all very proper.
[us] We wanted it done the way your people do it.
[them] It was noticed.
[them] One of ours is in your cells, I hear.
[us] They are, and they're fed and kept warm.
[them,their:lowtech] My people would like them back by their own fire.
[them] My people would like them back.
[us] Then your people can make us an offer.
[them] You hold one of ours, and I'm still standing here talking to you.
[us] We can talk about that too, if your people want to.
[us] Your people hold one of ours.
[them] I know, and I'm not the one who decides it.
[us] Then tell whoever does that we want them back.
[them] I'll tell them, for what it's worth.
[them] I remember the inside of your cells at {CAPTOR}.
[us] I hope you remember the day you walked out too.
[them] I do, which is why I'm talking to you at all.
[them] When I was held at {CAPTOR}, your people fed me better than I expected.
[us] We try to.
[them] I told them so at home.
[them] I haven't forgotten the cells at {CAPTOR}.
[us] Neither have we.
